heading: SEBI's Performance-Linked Fee vs. TER: What It Means for Your Mutual Funds
tldr: SEBI has proposed a new framework to link mutual fund fees directly to a scheme's performance.
This model aims to replace or supplement the existing Total Expense Ratio (TER) system.
Under the proposed system, fund managers would earn higher fees for outperforming a benchmark and potentially lower fees for underperformance.
Mutual fund houses are expressing concerns due to operational complexities and potential revenue volatility.
The move seeks to better align the interests of fund managers with those of investors, promoting merit-based compensation.
caption:
Big news for your mutual funds! India's market regulator wants to change how fund managers get paid. Instead of a fixed fee, they might earn more if your fund does well, and less if it doesn't. This could mean better value for your money and smarter investing decisions. Want to know how this impacts your savings? Read the full article to understand more.
